newsitem.title: UK: Zambian doctor faces charges for working with HIV.
newsitem.headline: Zambian doctor faces charges for working with HIV.

text.p: A Zambian-born doctor failed to turn up for a disciplinary hearing on Monday to face charges of professional misconduct for continuing to treat patients when he knew he was HIV positive.
Lawyers for gynaecologist Patrick Ngosa told Britain's General Medical Council he denied the charge and said he had not turned up for the hearing because he feared being identified.
They said Ngosa has been subjected to a "witch hunt" by the media since last week, when the hospital where he worked appealed to women he had treated to make contact.
"He was scared for himself and he was scared for his family," Ngosa's lawyer, Nicola Davies, said.
The hearing was told that Ngosa learned he was carrying the deadly virus from a woman with whom he had a two-year affair and who was named only as Mrs A in court.

Mrs A told him that she was HIV positive in May 1996, but Ngosa denied to hospital officials that he had had an affair with her. He did not himself have an HIV test until several months later and then did not tell the hospital of the result until January this year.
More than 7,000 women have contacted a hotline for Ngosa's former patients at hospitals in Gloucester in central England, and Essex, east of London.
The hospitals had identified around 1,700 women they feared were slightly at risk because they had received invasive surgical treatment from Ngosa.
But they stressed the risk is tiny. There are only two cases worldwide of people contracting the HIV virus from health care workers.
The hearing was adjourned until Tuesday.
